analysis.summary: The PR fragments VAT validation by replacing a general validator with specific 'Personal' or 'Company' ones without maintaining the 'OR' logic in UI components, which will cause valid VAT numbers to be rejected in various customer flows.

bugs.title: Restrictive VAT validation in AddressDetailsForm
bugs.description: The component now strictly uses 'validateCompnayVATNumber' (Company) for validation. This form is shared with B2C (Personal) flows, but unlike the BFF which checks both types, this UI check will fail for personal VAT formats.
bugs.risk: High severity: B2C customers will be blocked from completing their address details if they provide a personal VAT number, as the UI will incorrectly mark it as invalid and potentially block checkout progression.

bugs.title: Incomplete VAT validation logic in form utility
bugs.description: The form validation utility now strictly uses 'validatePersonalVATNumber'. In scenarios where 'enableEditableVatField' is active for SME (Company) users, their company VAT numbers will fail this personal-only check and prevent form submission.
bugs.risk: High severity: SME customers with editable VAT fields will be unable to submit the form because their valid company VAT numbers are being validated against the personal VAT format, resulting in a hard block on the frontend.

notBugs.reason: While 'Compnay' is a spelling error, it is used consistently across BFF and Frontend import and call sites, indicating it likely matches the exported name in the updated @smart/utils library version 9.28.0.
Speculative; although 'data.body' is used on Line 109, the definition of 'data' likely exists in the omitted lines of the handler function and would be caught by standard linting.
